title: 4B Setup
teaches: The 4B- (Stan Weinstein) as we trade it: after a Stage 4 decline under a falling 30-week line, a stock that has seen its low for the cycle sets a higher low on drying volume, reclaims the 50-day and pauses above it with room to run, the buy is the trade through the pause high at market once price is back above the 200-day and never more than 4% past it, the trade is short term on our trims with no adding, and a plain 4B that is still falling is much too soon to buy.

questions.q: In Weinstein's stage legend, what does a plain 4B mean?
choices: Late in the decline: not a buy yet
A bottom is in: buy on strength
Early in the decline: sell rallies
A Stage 2 breakout on volume
questions.answer: Late in the decline: not a buy yet
questions.why: Late in the downtrend, and much too soon to consider buying. The buy is the 4B-, the one with the minus.
questions.lesson_line: A plain 4B is not a buy. Wait for the minus.

wrong.A bottom is in: buy on strength: That is the minus. A plain 4B is late in the downtrend and much too soon to consider buying.
wrong.Early in the decline: sell rallies: The B means late in the stage, not early.
wrong.A Stage 2 breakout on volume: Stage 2 is the advance. A plain 4B is still the declining stage, and there is no reason to be long.

questions.q: What does the minus in 4B- say?
choices: The low for the cycle is now in
The stock is still falling hard
The stock is already in Stage 2
The stock is a short candidate
questions.answer: The low for the cycle is now in
questions.why: The stock has now seen its low for the cycle. It is not yet officially in Stage 1A, but the low is in.
questions.lesson_line: The minus says the low is in. Not yet a base, but the low is in.

wrong.The stock is still falling hard: That is a plain 4B. The minus says the low for the cycle is in.
wrong.The stock is already in Stage 2: It is not yet even officially in Stage 1A. The minus only says the low is in.
wrong.The stock is a short candidate: The minus says the low for the cycle is in, so it is a long idea, not a short.

questions.why: True. A Stage 4 decline comes first: at the low the 150-day, the 30-week line, was falling and price was under it.

questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. It is a short-term trade on the house trims: one price, one stop, no adding along the way.
questions.lesson_line: In and out on our trims. One price, one stop, no adds.

questions.q: A 4B- needs a close back above the 50-day average.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. The close is above the 50-day, the recapture of the 50-day that Weinstein names.
questions.lesson_line: The 50-day has to be won back before the buy.

questions.q: We do not buy a 4B- while the close is still under the 200-day.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. No longs below the 200-day simple moving average, unless it is a parabolic long.
questions.lesson_line: Under the 200-day, no long. Get back above it first.

questions.q: How is the cycle low found?
choices: Lowest low of the 252 sessions before
Lowest close of the last 20 sessions
The 50-day average at its lowest point
The day with the most volume traded
questions.answer: Lowest low of the 252 sessions before
questions.why: The lowest low of the 252 sessions before the trigger, our working rule. The 52-week high is the highest high of the 252 sessions before the cycle low.
questions.lesson_line: Find the cycle low first. Everything else is measured from it.

wrong.Lowest close of the last 20 sessions: That is a recent dip, not the low for the cycle. The cycle low looks back 252 sessions.
wrong.The 50-day average at its lowest point: An average is not the low. The cycle low is the lowest low of the 252 sessions.
wrong.The day with the most volume traded: Volume does not pick the low. The lowest low of the 252 sessions does.

questions.q: How far above the cycle low should the higher low sit?
choices: At least 3%
At least 15%
Any amount, even equal
At least 1%
questions.answer: At least 3%
questions.why: At least 3%, set at least 10 sessions after the cycle low, after a rally of 5% or more. That is our working rule for a higher low.
questions.lesson_line: A higher low is a real step up, not a tie.

wrong.At least 15%: That asks for far too much. Our working rule is 3%.
wrong.Any amount, even equal: An equal low is not higher. The higher low has to sit at least 3% above.
wrong.At least 1%: 1% is too little. Our working rule is 3%.

questions.q: How many closes above the 50-day make the minimum pause?
questions.why: 2 closes above the 50-day before the trigger is our working minimum. A pause of 5 to 20 sessions did best in our test.
questions.lesson_line: Two closes above the 50-day is the minimum pause.

wrong.1: One close is a single day above the average, not a pause.
wrong.5: 5 sessions did well, but the minimum is 2.
wrong.10: 10 sessions is a longer pause. The minimum is 2.

questions.q: We take a 4B- in a $5 stock that trades $20 million a day.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. The price must be $10 or more, and at least $20 million has to trade a day.
questions.lesson_line: Under $10 is out, however clean the base.

questions.q: What is the buy on a 4B-?
choices: Trades over the pause high, at market
The first daily close over the 50-day
A limit order at the new higher low
A close over the 200-day average
questions.answer: Trades over the pause high, at market
questions.why: It trades over the highest high of the pause above the 50-day, during regular hours, bought at market. That is our default trigger.
questions.lesson_line: Over the pause high, in hours, at market.

wrong.The first daily close over the 50-day: The 50-day reclaim comes first. The buy waits for the pause and the trade over its high.
wrong.A limit order at the new higher low: A limit at the higher low buys before the pause is built. Entries are market orders.
wrong.A close over the 200-day average: Being over the 200-day is a gate, not the trigger. The trigger is the pause high.

questions.q: A buy 12 sessions after the cycle low is long enough for a 4B-.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. Our working rule needs at least 15 sessions from the cycle low to the trigger, so 12 is still too early.
questions.lesson_line: Give the base time. At least 15 sessions off the low.

questions.q: Bought at 22.12 with the stop at 21.49. Where is 3R?
questions.why: 24.01. One R is the fill minus the stop. Add three of those to the fill. This is PENN's buy.
questions.lesson_line: Know your 3R before the open. The first third comes off there.

questions.q: The 52-week high is 60.00 and the cycle low is 31.50. How far under the high is the low, in percent?
questions.why: 47.5%. The high minus the low, divided by the high.
questions.lesson_line: Depth is high minus low, over the high. Measure it.

questions.q: The cycle low is 20.00 and the higher low is 21.40. How far above the cycle low is it, in percent?
questions.why: 7%. The higher low over the cycle low, minus one. Our working rule wants at least 3%.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the step up from the cycle low.

questions.q: Volume on the down days into the higher low should dry up.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Our working rule: the down days of the higher-low pullback trade below the 50-day average volume.
questions.lesson_line: Quiet selling into the higher low is the picture.

questions.q: How much room do we want to the nearest overhead level?
choices: At least 3R
At least 1R
Any room at all
At least 10R
questions.answer: At least 3R
questions.why: At least 3R from the entry to the nearest overhead level, counting only levels above the entry.
questions.lesson_line: Three R of room, or the trade is not worth it.

wrong.At least 1R: 1R does not reach the first trim at 3R. The room has to be 3R.
wrong.Any room at all: A wall just overhead is the named mistake. We want 3R.
wrong.At least 10R: 10R is far more than the first trim needs. The line is 3R.

questions.q: A fresh reason for the turn, like an earnings reaction, counts against a 4B-.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. A fresh reason for the turn, like an earnings reaction or a guidance change, helps. Keep the buy out of the 3 days before a report.
questions.lesson_line: A fresh reason for the turn helps the setup.

questions.q: After entry, the stop is the exit.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. The stop is the exit. It only moves up, never down or wider.
questions.lesson_line: The stop is the plan. It only moves up.

questions.q: Buy the open?
questions.story: The pause high is 40.00. The stock gaps open at 42.00.
choices: Pass; 5% past the pause high
Buy at market; it is so strong
Buy half size at the open
questions.answer: Pass; 5% past the pause high
questions.why: Pass. Skip if already more than 4% above the trigger level; this is 5% over. Chasing costs size, because the stop stays put.
questions.lesson_line: More than 4% past the pause high is no trade.

wrong.Buy at market; it is so strong: Past 4% the stop stays far away and the shares shrink. That is a chase.
wrong.Buy half size at the open: Half of a chase is still a chase. The line is 4%.

questions.q: Buy it?
questions.story: A stock down 60% still makes new lows under a falling 30-week line. It looks cheap.
choices: No; that stock is a plain 4B
Yes; it is cheap, down 60%
Yes, but only a small starter
questions.answer: No; that stock is a plain 4B
questions.why: No. Never a 4B without the minus. A stock still making new lows is much too soon to consider buying.
questions.lesson_line: Cheap is not a reason. A falling stock is a falling stock.

wrong.Yes; it is cheap, down 60%: Buying because it seems cheap is the named mistake.
wrong.Yes, but only a small starter: Size does not fix timing. It is much too soon to consider buying.

questions.q: What does that tell you?
questions.story: A stock bounces for three weeks, then closes under its cycle low.
choices: The low call was wrong; still a 4
A bargain; buy more on the dip
A higher low; the setup is now on
questions.answer: The low call was wrong; still a 4
questions.why: The low-for-the-cycle call was wrong. It is still a 4B or a 4.
questions.lesson_line: A close under the cycle low resets the count.

wrong.A bargain; buy more on the dip: A close under the cycle low is no bargain. The low was not the low.
wrong.A higher low; the setup is now on: A higher low sits above the cycle low. This closed under it.

questions.q: Buy the break?
questions.story: A 4B- shape: a higher low, a 50-day reclaim and a pause. The close is still 12% under the 200-day.
choices: No; no longs under the 200-day
Yes; the shape is perfect
Yes, on half size
questions.answer: No; no longs under the 200-day
questions.why: No. No longs below the 200-day simple moving average, unless it is a parabolic long. Wait until price is back above it.
questions.lesson_line: The shape is not enough. The 200-day comes first.

wrong.Yes; the shape is perfect: A perfect shape under the 200-day is still under the 200-day.
wrong.Yes, on half size: Half size does not change the 200-day rule.

questions.q: Bought at 12.37, stop 12.06. The stock trades to 13.92. How many R is that?
questions.why: 5R. Each R is the fill minus the stop. That is where the second third comes off. This is AMD's buy.
questions.lesson_line: Count in R, not dollars. 5R is the second trim.

questions.q: The stop moves to breakeven at 1R, well before the first trim.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. Stop to breakeven between 2R and 5R, at the first trim by default.
questions.lesson_line: Breakeven between 2R and 5R, at the first trim.

questions.q: In our test, which pause above the 50-day did worst?
choices: A bare 2 to 4 session pause
A pause of 5 to 10 sessions
A pause of 11 to 20 sessions
A pause of 21 to 40 sessions
questions.answer: A bare 2 to 4 session pause
questions.why: A bare 2 to 4 session pause: 15.7% reached 3R. The 5 to 10 session pause did best, at 25.9%.
questions.lesson_line: Give the pause a few days. A bare two-day pause did worst.

wrong.A pause of 11 to 20 sessions: 23.1% reached 3R, well above the bare pause.
wrong.A pause of 21 to 40 sessions: 21.3% reached 3R, also above the bare pause.

questions.q: Which group reading helps a 4B-?
choices: The group ETF closes above its 50-day
The group ETF falls hardest on the day
The group is not part of the 4B- call
questions.answer: The group ETF closes above its 50-day
questions.why: The stock's group ETF or index closing above its own 50-day. It helps most when the group is basing too and the stock is among the first to reclaim its 50-day.
questions.lesson_line: A turning group lifts a turning stock.

wrong.The group ETF falls hardest on the day: A group falling hardest is the weak end. We want the group turning up too.
wrong.The group is not part of the 4B- call: A weak group is a named mistake. The group turning up helps.

questions.q: What does that do to the setup?
questions.story: A stock sets a higher low, then closes under it two weeks before the pause is done.
choices: It is off; the higher low failed
It is on; a fresh low is cheaper
Nothing; only the cycle low counts
questions.answer: It is off; the higher low failed
questions.why: It is off. Under our working rule, a close under the higher low before the entry cancels the setup.
questions.lesson_line: A higher low that breaks is not a higher low.

wrong.It is on; a fresh low is cheaper: A close under the higher low cancels the setup. A lower low is not a bargain.
wrong.Nothing; only the cycle low counts: A close under the cycle low also cancels it, but a close under the higher low does too.

questions.q: Is that a 4B-?
questions.story: A stock undercuts its low and reclaims it two sessions later. You want to buy the reclaim.
choices: No; a 4B- waits for a higher low
Yes; it reclaimed the old low fast
Yes, if the reclaim volume is big
questions.answer: No; a 4B- waits for a higher low
questions.why: No. A 4B- never closes under its cycle low. It waits 15 or more sessions for a higher low, a 50-day reclaim and a pause before the buy.
questions.lesson_line: An undercut and reclaim is quick. A 4B- takes weeks.

wrong.Yes; it reclaimed the old low fast: That is a different setup that buys a quick reclaim. A 4B- never closes under its cycle low.
wrong.Yes, if the reclaim volume is big: Volume does not make a quick reclaim into a 4B-. The 4B- waits for the base.

questions.q: Is that a 4B-?
questions.story: A stock flushes on twice its usual volume under every fast average. You buy the snap back two days later.
choices: No; a capitulation snap back
Yes; it flushed hard to the low
Yes, if it holds the new low
questions.answer: No; a capitulation snap back
questions.why: No. A capitulation buys the snap back within 3 sessions of a flush. A 4B- waits weeks for a higher low on drying volume and a 50-day reclaim.
questions.lesson_line: A snap back is quick. A 4B- takes weeks.

wrong.Yes; it flushed hard to the low: A flush buys the snap back. A 4B- waits for the base.
wrong.Yes, if it holds the new low: Holding the low is not enough. A 4B- waits for a higher low and a 50-day reclaim.

questions.q: Is it a 4B- yet?
questions.story: A stock bottoms and rallies straight into its 50-day with no pullback.
choices: No; it has no higher low
Yes; it reclaimed the 50-day
Yes, on lower volume
questions.answer: No; it has no higher low
questions.why: No. A higher low is the critical signal, and a V straight up into the 50-day has not shown one.
questions.lesson_line: No pullback, no higher low, no 4B- yet.

wrong.Yes; it reclaimed the 50-day: The 50-day reclaim is one step. Without a higher low, it is a V.
wrong.Yes, on lower volume: Volume cannot stand in for a higher low.

questions.q: Take it?
questions.story: You would buy at 50.00 with the stop at 48.50. The falling 150-day sits at 52.00, just overhead.
choices: Pass; only 1.33R of room
Take it; the 200-day will break
Take it, on half size
questions.answer: Pass; only 1.33R of room
questions.why: Pass. Our working rule wants at least 3R to the nearest overhead level, and the falling 150-day leaves only 1.33R.
questions.lesson_line: A wall just overhead is no trade. Count the room.

wrong.Take it; the 200-day will break: Buying right under a falling long average with less than 3R of room is the named mistake.
wrong.Take it, on half size: Half size does not buy more room.

questions.q: Buy the break?
questions.story: A clean pause break sets up for tomorrow. The company reports after the close in 2 days.
choices: No; no buys 3 sessions before a report
Yes; the shape is clean
Yes, and sell before the report
questions.answer: No; no buys 3 sessions before a report
questions.why: No. No new buy in the 3 sessions before a report. Hold through a report only if up 5R.
questions.lesson_line: Check the report date before every buy.

wrong.Yes; the shape is clean: A clean shape does not move the earnings window.
wrong.Yes, and sell before the report: The rule is no new buy in that window, not a quick trade through it.

questions.q: Buy the break?
questions.story: A pause breaks out, and the stock sits 12% over its 10-day average.
choices: No; too far over the 10-day
Yes; the break itself is clean
Yes, but only on half size
questions.answer: No; too far over the 10-day
questions.why: No. Skip if more than 10% above the 10-day average. This one is 12% over.
questions.lesson_line: A clean break, too far above its average, is a pass.

wrong.Yes; the break itself is clean: The break is clean, but the stretch rule comes before the break.
wrong.Yes, but only on half size: Half size does not cure a stretch.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: You bought a 4B- break 10 trading days ago. It sits at 0.7R, drifting under the falling 200-day.
choices: Sell; under 1R after 10 days
Hold; the stop has not traded
Add; it is cheap
questions.answer: Sell; under 1R after 10 days
questions.why: Sell. A trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold, freeing the money.
questions.lesson_line: Ten days and nothing. The money has somewhere better to be.

wrong.Hold; the stop has not traded: The time stop is its own exit. Under 1R after 10 days, the money goes elsewhere.
wrong.Add; it is cheap: Adding along the way is the named mistake. One price, one stop.

questions.q: Buy it, or stand aside?
questions.story: A clean 4B- breaks the pause high, but the market reading just turned Red.
choices: No new long; Red is mostly cash
Buy; the base is great and clean
Buy half size, tight stop
questions.answer: No new long; Red is mostly cash
questions.why: No new long. Red is mostly cash and shorts, and a 4B- is a long. Existing trades keep their stops.
questions.lesson_line: A great base in a Red market still waits.

wrong.Buy; the base is great and clean: Buying against the market is the named mistake. Red is mostly cash.
wrong.Buy half size, tight stop: Half size is still a new long in a Red market.

questions.q: What now?
questions.story: A stock has reclaimed its 50-day and paused for a week. Today it closes back under the 50-day.
choices: Wait for a new 2-session pause
Buy the dip; it is cheaper now
Move the stop down to the 200-day
questions.answer: Wait for a new 2-session pause
questions.why: Wait for a new pause. A close back under the 50-day before the trigger re-arms the setup only after a new 2-session pause above it.
questions.lesson_line: Lost the 50-day, so wait for a fresh pause above it.

wrong.Buy the dip; it is cheaper now: The setup is off until a new pause forms. A dip under the 50-day is no entry.
wrong.Move the stop down to the 200-day: There is no position yet, and the 200-day is not the stop.

questions.q: Account 50,000. Risk 1%. Buy 22.12, stop 21.49. How many shares?
questions.why: 793. Account times risk percent, divided by the buy minus the stop, rounded down. The stop sets the size.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first, distance second, size last.

questions.q: How do you play the open?
questions.story: You bought at 40.00 with the stop at 39.00, so 3R is 43.00. The next morning it opens at 43.60.
choices: Take a third off at the open
Wait for the close to decide
Sell it all and take the gain
questions.answer: Take a third off at the open
questions.why: Sell a third at the open. A trim level the day opens past is taken at the open.
questions.lesson_line: Take the trim the open hands you.

wrong.Wait for the close to decide: The level is already passed. Waiting gives the gap time to fill.
wrong.Sell it all and take the gain: A third at 3R. The rest waits for 5R and the trail.

questions.q: What now?
questions.story: You bought at 40.00 with the stop at 39.00. It gaps open at 38.20, and the first 30-minute low is 37.80.
choices: Out now; the loss is past the 2R cap
The new stop is the 37.80 low
Hold; gaps tend to fill in time
questions.answer: Out now; the loss is past the 2R cap
questions.why: Out. On a gap through the stop the first 30-minute low is the new stop, but past 2R you get out. A low of 37.80 is more than 2R from 40.00.
questions.lesson_line: A gap through the stop has a ceiling of 2R.

wrong.The new stop is the 37.80 low: The 30-minute low is the stop only while the loss is inside 2R. This one is past it.
wrong.Hold; gaps tend to fill in time: Hope is not a rule. The gap rule has a ceiling, and this is past it.

questions.q: What now?
questions.story: You hold the last third of a fast mover after both trims. Today it closes under its 10-day.
choices: Sell the last third on that close
Hold until the 50-day breaks down
Move the stop down to the 50-day
questions.answer: Sell the last third on that close
questions.why: Sell the last third. A fast mover trails the 10-day, and we sell on a close below it.
questions.lesson_line: The trail is a close under the 10-day. Sell it.

wrong.Hold until the 50-day breaks down: The trail is the 10-day for a fast mover, not the 50-day.
wrong.Move the stop down to the 50-day: The stop only moves up, never down or wider.

questions.q: How do you answer them?
questions.story: Your 4B- trade is working. A friend says to add along the way, as some traders do.
choices: No; one price, one stop, no adds
Yes; add on each fresh higher low
Yes, but only add half the size
questions.answer: No; one price, one stop, no adds
questions.why: No. Size from the stop; one price, one stop, no adding along the way. Adding on the way up is the named mistake.
questions.lesson_line: Full size once. A winner is not a reason to add.

wrong.Yes; add on each fresh higher low: Adding to it on the way up is the named mistake.
wrong.Yes, but only add half the size: A smaller add is still an add with a second price and a second stop.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: You are up 4R in four days on a vertical, wide-range burst.
choices: Sell a big part into the burst
Add; it is going parabolic
Hold it all; the trail will handle it
questions.answer: Sell a big part into the burst
questions.why: Sell a big part into it. A climax run on your own long is for selling into; how much is a judgment call.
questions.lesson_line: A vertical burst is for selling into.

wrong.Add; it is going parabolic: Adding is the named mistake, and a burst is for selling into.
wrong.Hold it all; the trail will handle it: The trail catches the turn late. A burst is the moment to bank a big part.

questions.q: Our position can be up to 5% of the stock's average daily volume.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. Never own more than 1% of a stock's average daily volume.
questions.lesson_line: Size to the stock's volume, not just the stop.

questions.q: How does the market change the buy?
questions.story: After a broad market decline the index turns up. A stock is among the first in its group to reclaim its 50-day.
choices: Good; start with a few positions
Wait; the market must make a new high
Go all in on this one
questions.answer: Good; start with a few positions
questions.why: Good conditions. The best turns come once the market itself turns up. After a correction, start with a few positions and add more only as they work.
questions.lesson_line: A market turning up is the wind behind the turn.

wrong.Wait; the market must make a new high: The best turns come when the market itself turns back up, not after a new high.
wrong.Go all in on this one: After a correction, start with a few positions and add more only as the first ones work.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: Your 4B- stalls under the falling 200-day and slides toward the old low. A friend says to hold it as an investment.
choices: Sell by the rules; never hold Stage 4
Hold it; it is a long-term bottom
Add to it; it is cheaper
questions.answer: Sell by the rules; never hold Stage 4
questions.why: Sell by the rules. A 4B- is a short-term trade. Holding it as an investment, back into Stage 4, is the named mistake.
questions.lesson_line: Do not turn a short-term trade into an investment.

wrong.Hold it; it is a long-term bottom: Holding a short-term trade back down into Stage 4 is the named mistake.
wrong.Add to it; it is cheaper: Adding is the named mistake, and the stop is the exit.

questions.q: The stop traded. Was the loss a mistake?
questions.story: You bought a 4B- at 12.99 with the stop at 12.59. A 37.5% decline, a higher low, a 12-day pause. The next session fell to 12.48.
choices: No; a planned loss, stop did its job
Yes; the stop was too tight
Yes; we bought too late
questions.answer: No; a planned loss, stop did its job
questions.why: No. The stop is the plan, and the loss was the planned 3.1%. A correct-looking 4B- can still lose.
questions.lesson_line: A correct setup can lose. The stop makes it small.

wrong.Yes; the stop was too tight: The stop sits where the rules put it. Widening it to dodge a loss is the mistake.
wrong.Yes; we bought too late: The buy was at the pause high, not a chase.

questions.q: After the first stop-out, when do you buy again?
questions.story: A 39% drop to the March 2020 low, a higher low, a 13-day pause. The break took the 1.4% stop the next day.
choices: Only on a new trigger, as a new trade
At once; it is the same setup
Never again on this stock
questions.answer: Only on a new trigger, as a new trade
questions.why: Only on a new trigger. After a stop-out, buy again only if the setup triggers again, as a new trade. META's second trigger also stopped; the real move came from a third base.
questions.lesson_line: A V bottom can fail twice. Only a new trigger buys it again.

wrong.At once; it is the same setup: After a stop-out, buy again only on a new trigger, as a new trade.
wrong.Never again on this stock: The setup can trigger again. The real move came from a third base.

questions.q: What grade cue flagged this one?
questions.story: MSFT, 2001: a 66% Stage 4 decline, a 92-session base, an 18-day pause. The break reached a fraction of 1R, then the stop.
choices: A falling 200-day over the trade
The pause was too long
The base was too short
questions.answer: A falling 200-day over the trade
questions.why: A falling 200-day over the trade. The long averages should be flat or turning, not still falling steeply.
questions.lesson_line: Watch the long averages. A falling 200-day is overhead supply.

wrong.The pause was too long: An 18-day pause is inside the 5 to 20 sessions that did best.
wrong.The base was too short: A 92-session base is long. The falling long average was the cue.

questions.q: Which check could have kept you out?
questions.story: Two 4B- triggers in a bear market, months apart. Each looked clean, and each stopped the next session.
choices: The market reading
A tighter stop
A bigger position
questions.answer: The market reading
questions.why: The market reading. Two 4B- triggers in the 2008 bear were both stopped without trading above the entry. Buying against the market is a named mistake.
questions.lesson_line: Forest first, then the trees. Check the market.

wrong.A tighter stop: A tighter stop would have been hit even sooner. The missing filter was the market.
wrong.A bigger position: More size on a losing setup only loses more.

questions.q: Is it a 4B-?
questions.story: A stock drops 34% from its high. At the cycle low the 150-day was rising: 528.74 against 521.41 twenty sessions earlier.
choices: No; a pullback in an uptrend
Yes; the drop is deep enough
Yes, if volume dried up
questions.answer: No; a pullback in an uptrend
questions.why: No. A 34% drop under a 150-day that was still rising at the low is a pullback in an uptrend. That is a Remount or a pullback buy, not a Stage 4 turn.
questions.lesson_line: Read the 150-day at the low before you name it.

wrong.Yes; the drop is deep enough: A deep drop is not a Stage 4. The 150-day was rising at the low.
wrong.Yes, if volume dried up: Dry volume does not change a rising 150-day at the low.

questions.q: Is that a real higher low?
questions.story: A V off a low. The higher low sits 6.8% above the cycle low, but the best high off the low was only 4.1% above it.
choices: No; no 5% rally before it, so one leg
Yes; it is above the cycle low
Yes, if volume dried up
questions.answer: No; no 5% rally before it, so one leg
questions.why: No. Our working rule puts a rally of 5% or more before the higher low. Here the best high off the low was only 4.1% above it, so it is one leg, not a base.
questions.lesson_line: A higher low needs a rally before it. Otherwise it is one leg.

wrong.Yes; it is above the cycle low: Above the cycle low is not enough. A rally of 5% or more has to come before it.
wrong.Yes, if volume dried up: Dry volume does not make one leg into a base.

questions.q: Does our earnings rule allow that buy?
questions.story: A vendor's example buys a 50-day reclaim at 189 on 2022-07-15 or 2022-07-18. The company reports after the close on 2022-07-19.
choices: No; within 3 sessions of the report
Yes; the reclaim was clean
Yes, if it holds the 50-day
questions.answer: No; within 3 sessions of the report
questions.why: No. No new buy in the 3 sessions before a report. That 50-day reclaim was bought one to two sessions before the report.
questions.lesson_line: Check the report date, even on a famous chart.

wrong.Yes; the reclaim was clean: A clean reclaim does not move the earnings window.
wrong.Yes, if it holds the 50-day: Holding the 50-day does not change the report date.

questions.q: Write the plan.
questions.story: NUS, April 2013: 78 sessions off a December low, a February higher low, and a 19-day pause above a turning 50-day.
choices: Buy 49.99, stop 49.05, a third at 3R
Buy 49.99, stop 45.00, hold it all
Wait for a Stage 2 breakout instead
questions.answer: Buy 49.99, stop 49.05, a third at 3R
questions.why: Buy at market, 49.99, once price trades over the pause high. Stop 49.05, 1.9% away. A third comes off at 3R.
questions.lesson_line: Entry, stop, trim, trail. Write it before the open.

wrong.Buy 49.99, stop 45.00, hold it all: The stop here sat 1.9% away; 45.00 is far wider. And a third comes off at 3R.
wrong.Wait for a Stage 2 breakout instead: That is a different trade. This is the 4B-, the short-term play.

questions.q: Which gets the bigger size?
questions.story: Two 4B- breaks. A: a clean higher low, a tight pause on a flat 50-day, the group and market turning up. B: no higher low, a steeply falling 50-day, an old level just overhead.
choices: A; every cue lines up
B; it has more upside
Equal; both broke out
questions.answer: A; every cue lines up
questions.why: A. A clean higher low, a tight pause on a flat 50-day, and a group and market turning up are the A+ end. No higher low, a steeply falling 50-day and an old level just overhead are the B- end.
questions.lesson_line: Same setup, different grade. The base and the backdrop set the size.

wrong.B; it has more upside: B has a wall overhead and no higher low. Its room is the problem.
wrong.Equal; both broke out: Both broke the pause high, but the base and the backdrop differ.

questions.q: Did the system break?
questions.story: You take five 4B- trades by the rules. Four stop out, and one runs for 5R.
choices: No; about one in five reaches 3R
Yes; the setup does not work
Yes; widen the stops
questions.answer: No; about one in five reaches 3R
questions.why: No. In our test above the 200-day, 22.2% of 4B- hits reached 3R before a fixed stop. So four stops in five is ordinary. Keep stops small and take the trims when one works.
questions.lesson_line: A 4B- loses often. Small stops and trims keep it alive.

wrong.Yes; the setup does not work: A low hit rate with small stops and trims is the design, not a failure.
wrong.Yes; widen the stops: Widening the stop is the mistake. A small, fixed stop is what keeps the losses small.

questions.q: In Bulkowski's own trades, Stage 4 buys made money about 24% of the time.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Bulkowski's own Stage 4 buys made money 24% of the time, so a 4B- is a low-hit-rate trade that lives on small stops and trims.
questions.lesson_line: Buying near a Stage 4 low is a low-odds trade. Trade it small and short.

questions.q: Hidden ticker. A washout, a higher low, a pause over the 50-day. Above its 200-day? Take it or pass.
choices: Take it; above the 200-day, higher low
Pass; the 200-day is overhead
Pass; there is no higher low
questions.answer: Take it; above the 200-day, higher low
questions.why: Take it. A spring washout, a higher low, and an 11-day pause that walked up through the 50, 150 and 200-day lines. The prior close was above the 200-day. It ran past 5R within two weeks.
questions.lesson_line: The 200-day first, then the base. Both passed here.

wrong.Pass; the 200-day is overhead: Look again: price sits above the 200-day here.
wrong.Pass; there is no higher low: Look again: the second low sits well above the first.

questions.q: Hidden ticker. A deep decline, a higher low, a 50-day reclaim. Is it above the 200-day? Take it or pass.
choices: Pass; it is still under the 200-day
Take it; the base is textbook
Take it; the higher low is big
questions.answer: Pass; it is still under the 200-day
questions.why: Pass. The close was 10.2% under the 200-day the day before the trigger. A base can work and still not be ours: no longs under the 200-day.
questions.lesson_line: The shape is not enough. The 200-day decides.

wrong.Take it; the base is textbook: The base is textbook, but the close is under the 200-day. That rule comes first.
wrong.Take it; the higher low is big: A big higher low does not lift a close over the 200-day.

questions.q: Which one do we take?
questions.story: Four candidates today. A: still making new lows. B: the close is under the 200-day. C: a higher low, a pause over the 50-day, 3R of room. D: reports in 2 days.
choices: A; it is the cheapest
B; the pause is longest
C; a higher low and room to run
D; it has the freshest reason
questions.answer: C; a higher low and room to run
questions.why: C. A plain 4B still making new lows, a close under the 200-day and a report inside 3 sessions each rule one out. C has the higher low and the room.
questions.lesson_line: Run every gate. One failure ends it.

wrong.A; it is the cheapest: A stock still making new lows is a plain 4B, much too soon to buy.
wrong.B; the pause is longest: Under the 200-day, no longs. A long pause does not change that.
wrong.D; it has the freshest reason: A report inside 3 sessions ends it, however fresh the reason.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: After a correction, start with a few positions and add more only as the first ones ___.
questions.answer: work
questions.why: Work. After a correction, start with a few positions and add more only as the first ones work.
questions.lesson_line: Start small after a correction. Let the first positions earn the next ones.

questions.q: Do you take the third one?
questions.story: A broad selloff ends and the market reading turns Green again. You hold two 4B- trades, both past their first trim. A third 4B- triggers.
choices: Yes; the first two are working
No; wait for a new index high
Yes, by adding to the first two
questions.answer: Yes; the first two are working
questions.why: Yes. After a correction, start with a few positions and add more only as the first ones work. Yours are working.
questions.lesson_line: Add positions, not shares. Let the first ones prove the turn.

wrong.No; wait for a new index high: Our rule starts positions as the reading turns Green again. It does not wait for a new index high.
wrong.Yes, by adding to the first two: That adds to a trade. Our plan is one price, one stop, no adding along the way.

questions.q: Which stock earns the group cue on our card?
questions.story: Two stocks sit in one group, which is basing too. Both show the same higher low and pause above the 50-day. Stock A reclaimed its 50-day first. Stock B reclaimed it weeks later, after most of the group.
choices: Stock A, among the first to reclaim
Stock B, it waited for the group
Neither; the order is not part of it
questions.answer: Stock A, among the first to reclaim
questions.why: Stock A. Our card's cue is a basing group with the stock among the first in it to reclaim its 50-day.
questions.lesson_line: In a basing group, the early reclaimers earn the cue.

wrong.Stock B, it waited for the group: Stock B came late, after most of the group. The cue asks for among the first.
wrong.Neither; the order is not part of it: The cue is about the order. The stock should be among the first in the group to reclaim its 50-day.

questions.q: Which picture of the 150-day and 200-day lines is the better cue?
choices: Flat, or turning over the trade
Falling steeply, price far below
No difference to the grade
questions.answer: Flat, or turning over the trade
questions.why: Flat, or turning. Our card wants the 150-day and 200-day lines flat or turning over the trade, not still falling steeply.
questions.lesson_line: Flat or turning long averages are the better picture. A steep fall is not.

wrong.Falling steeply, price far below: TraderLion: a sharply falling average with the stock far below it has likely not yet entered a true Stage 1.
wrong.No difference to the grade: It is a cue that counts. Flat or turning lines are the better picture.

questions.q: A falling 200-day line cancels a 4B- on our card.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. The card calls flat or turning lines a cue. A steep fall grades worse, but a cue is not a veto.
questions.lesson_line: A falling long average is a weaker cue, not a rule that ends the setup.

questions.q: Do you buy now?
questions.story: Pre-market, a 4B- stock trades through its pause high of 20.00. The open is an hour away.
choices: No; wait for regular hours
Yes, with a market order
Yes, with a limit at 20.00
questions.answer: No; wait for regular hours
questions.why: No. Our entry is a market order once the trigger trades, and only during regular hours.
questions.lesson_line: Market order, regular hours only. A pre-market print is not a buy.

wrong.Yes, with a market order: A market order is our order type, but pre-market is outside regular hours.
wrong.Yes, with a limit at 20.00: Our entries are market orders, and pre-market is outside regular hours.

questions.q: Your planned stop level lands on exactly 25.00. Where does the stop go?
choices: A few cents under 25.00
Right on the 25.00 line
A few cents above 25.00
A full dollar under 25.00
questions.answer: A few cents under 25.00
questions.why: A few cents under 25.00. Our card keeps the stop off a round number: a few cents under it, not on it.
questions.lesson_line: A few cents under the round number, never right on it.

wrong.Right on the 25.00 line: Not on a round number. The stop sits a few cents under it.
wrong.A few cents above 25.00: That puts the stop above the level instead of under it. A long stop sits a few cents under.
wrong.A full dollar under 25.00: A few cents is the gap. A full dollar widens the stop and shrinks the size.

questions.q: Our card puts the stop right on the nearest round number.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. Not on a round number: a few cents under it.
questions.lesson_line: A few cents under the round number, not on it.

questions.q: What is wrong with that plan?
questions.story: You buy a 4B- and plan to sell by hand if it trades under your stop level. You place no stop order with your broker.
choices: Every position needs a real stop order
Nothing; you will be watching the screen
An alert is enough if you act fast
questions.answer: Every position needs a real stop order
questions.why: A stop kept in your head is not a stop. Every position has a real stop order with the broker.
questions.lesson_line: Place the order. A stop in your head is not a stop.

wrong.Nothing; you will be watching the screen: Watching is not an order. The stop sits with the broker even when you look away.
wrong.An alert is enough if you act fast: An alert is not an order. The rule is a real stop order with the broker.

questions.q: Our stop is a real order with the broker, and it only moves up.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. A real stop order with the broker, and it only moves up.
questions.lesson_line: Real order, with the broker. It only moves up.
